args.title: aca-redline.docx
args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
(Counterparty Draft v.2 Against Firm Base Materials / Depository Bank Standard Form)
Prepared for: [Client / Secured Party]
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (scenario-01)
Applicable materials reconciled: internal playbook; executed credit agreement; depository bank's standard form; account details; deal correspondence; schedules and exhibits. [Doc #58 is misfiled administrative correspondence and is NOT relied upon.]

NOTE ON FORMAT. Set out below is the tracked-changes redline of the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("ACA") against the required base positions. Text shown in [  ] denotes required INSERTIONS restoring the firm standard / base materials; text with strikethrough marks deletions that must be rejected (marked "REJ" in the margin is the counterparty's proposal that we refuse); text with double underlining and a "W-away" label identifies deviations the client treats as walk-away. Each change is cross-referenced to the issues/risk memorandum and the summary deviation matrix.

================================================================================
SECTION 2 — DEFINITIONS
================================================================================

2.1 "Material Adverse Effect." The counterparty's markup would amend the definition to read: 

[STRIKE: "Material Adverse Effect" means any change, event or development that has a material adverse effect on the business, results of operations or financial condition of the Grantor; PROVIDED that none of the following shall be deemed a Material Adverse Effect: (i) regulatory action of the type described in the pending inquiries referenced on Schedule 3.7, or any enforcement, investigation, subpoena or similar action commenced or threatened by any governmental authority in respect of the [collateral] accounts.]

[INS (restore firm standard — REJECT counterparty carve-outs): "Material Adverse Effect" means any change, event or development that has a material adverse effect on the business, results of operations or financial condition of the Grantor, without any carve-out for regulatory action. For the avoidance of doubt, no regulatory-action carve-out shall apply, and Schedule 3.7 shall not narrow the scope of this definition.]

RATIONALE: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries of exactly the kind the counterparty seeks to carve out. Adding the carve-out would strip the secured party of control protection precisely on the highest-exposure facts. The playbook requires that the MAE definition contain no regulatory-action carve-out and that disclosure schedule exceptions may not re-open the definition. (See issues memo Item 2.)

================================================================================
SECTION 5 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
================================================================================

5.1 Account details / subject accounts. {Account title, account number, ABA/routing number as set forth on the account details schedule.} [INS: Retain the account description schedule as Exhibit A; insert a representation that the account identified is the sole account subject to this ACA and that no other control agreement exists over the account at signing.]

5.2 No prior/conflicting control agreements. [INS (restore firm standard): Grantor and Depository Bank represent and warrant that no other account control agreement, deposit account control agreement or similar arrangement is in effect with respect to the Subject Account and that the Depository Bank has not executed any instruction or given any entitlement order inconsistent with this ACA. REJECT the counterparty's addition purporting to permit conflicting standby control agreements.]

RATIONALE: The counterparty's markup would permit the Depository Bank to honor competing instructions and would subvert the secured party's exclusive control under UCC § 9-104 and § 9-314. Schedule 5.2 retained-liability exposure is shifted by the indemnification changes (see SEC 7 below).

================================================================================
SECTION 6 — COVENANTS / INSTRUCTIONS AND CONTROL
================================================================================

6.1 Instructions. [INS (confirm firm standard): The Depository Bank agrees that it will comply with all instructions originated by the Secured Party, or its permitted designee, directing disposition of the funds in the Subject Account without further consent by the Grantor, and the Bank waives any requirement of a further entitlement order from the Grantor. REJECT counterparty's proposed condition requiring the Bank to obtain Grantor confirmation before honoring Secured Party instructions.]

6.2 No termination/removal. [INS: The Depository Bank will not terminate the Subject Account, change the account number, or transfer the account to another institution until the Secured Party has been provided the notice and control required by this Agreement and the executed credit agreement.]

================================================================================
SECTION 7 — INDEMNIFICATION
================================================================================

7.1 Indemnification cap. The counterparty's markup would reduce the aggregate indemnification cap from the firm-standard/base amount to [significantly lower amount] and convert the basket from a DEDUCTIBLE to a TIPPING basket, and would add a carve-out for Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.

[STRIKE — REJ (reject the reduced cap): "the aggregate liability of the [Grantor/Depository Bank] under this Section 7 shall not exceed [REDUCED CAP]."]

[STRIKE — REJ (reject retained-liability carve-out): "Indemnification obligations shall not extend to the retained liabilities described on Schedule 5.2."]

[INS (restore firm standard): "The aggregate liability of the [Grantor/Depository Bank] under this Section 7 shall not exceed [BASE / FIRM-STANDARD CAP]."]

[INS (concede basket mechanics per controlling partner instruction — retained): "The basket shall operate as a tipping basket (once the aggregate amount of covered losses equals or exceeds the basket threshold, the full amount, including the threshold, is recoverable), and the basket threshold shall be as set forth in the base materials."]

RATIONALE: The reduced cap and the Schedule 5.2 carve-out would silently shift retained liabilities to the Secured Party. By controlling instruction (deal correspondence, latest message), the client CONCEDES the conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket; the reduction of the aggregate cap and the Schedule 5.2 carve-out are REJECTED. (See issues memo Items 1 & 3.)

================================================================================
SECTION 8 — LIMITED UNDERTAKINGS / SURVIVAL
================================================================================

8.1 Survival period; limitation period. The counterparty's markup would add a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations and warranties.

[STRIKE — W-away (walk-away; REJECT): "No claim for breach of any representation, warranty or covenant under this Agreement may be brought after [SHORTENED PERIOD] from the date of this Agreement, notwithstanding anything in Exhibit B to the contrary."]

[INS (restore firm standard): "The representations, warranties and covenants and the indemnification obligations under this Agreement shall survive in accordance with the survival matrix set forth on Exhibit B, and no shorter limitation period shall apply."]

RATIONALE: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix that the counterparty's limitation-period change directly contradicts. The client treats any survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue per the controlling partner instruction; the deletion of this provision is mandatory. (See issues memo Item 4.)

================================================================================
SECTION 10 — GENERAL
================================================================================

10.1 Notices. [INS: Notices to the Depository Bank, Grantor and Secured Party as set forth in the account details, with the agreement that notices to the Bank regarding instructions and control be effective upon receipt, consistent with the executed credit agreement.]

10.2 Governing law & jurisdiction. [INS: Governed by the law of [state] consistent with the executed credit agreement and the Depositary Bank's standard form; the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts set forth in the executed credit agreement and, to the extent applicable, the UCC Article 9 control provisions.]

10.3 Entire agreement / no modification. [INS: This ACA may not be modified except by a written instrument executed by all parties; no course of dealing or usage of trade shall modify the control and instruction provisions.]

================================================================================
SUMMARY OF REDLINE CHANGES
================================================================================
(1) MAE definition — REJECT regulatory-action carve-outs; restore base definition. [Issues memo Item 2; HIGH risk]
(2) Indemnification cap — REJECT reduced cap and Schedule 5.2 carve-out; restore base cap. [Issue memo Item 1; HIGH risk]
(3) Basket — CONCEDE conversion to tipping basket per controlling instruction. [Issue memo Item 5; ACCEPTED]
(4) Survival/limitation period — REJECT shortened survival as a walk-away item; restore Exhibit B matrix. [Issue memo Item 4; HIGH / walk-away]
(5) Control/instruction provisions — REJECT condition requiring grantor confirmation; restore exclusive control standard.
(6) Missing protections inserted: no prior conflicting control agreements; notice; no unilateral account termination; governing law/jurisdiction tied to the executed credit agreement.

args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
ISSUES / RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Draft Review
Prepared for: [Client / Secured Party]
From: [Associate], on behalf of the deals/contracts group
Matter: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper (scenario-01)
Documents reviewed: internal contracting playbook; executed credit agreement; depository bank's standard form; account details schedule; counterparty markup (Doc #32); schedules and exhibits (Doc #84); deal correspondence (Doc #110). Doc #58 (administrative file) is misfiled/unrelated and was excluded.

PURPOSE & SOURCES OF TRUTH. We reconciled the counterparty's markup against (i) the internal playbook's standard positions, (ii) the executed credit agreement, (iii) the depository bank's standard form, (iv) the account details, and (v) the schedules/exhibits (which control over general statements in the base materials) and the controlling partner instruction. The controlling partner instruction (latest message in Doc #110) supersedes the earlier priority ordering and governs: the client will CONCEDE the basket conversion, but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.

================================================================================
I. DEVIATIONS, RISK RATINGS, AND RECOMMENDED POSITIONS
================================================================================

ITEM 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction (Section 7.1)  — RISK: HIGH
- Deviation: The counterparty's markup silently reduces the aggregate indemnification cap below the firm-standard/base amount and adds a carve-out excluding Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities (the retained liabilities list) from indemnification.
- Playbook requirement: The playbook standard requires the full base indemnification cap with no carve-out that removes scheduled retained liabilities from the secured party's protection; disclosure schedule exceptions may not serve as an end-run around the cap or scope.
- Exposure analysis: A reduced cap plus a Schedule 5.2 carve-out would strip the secured party of recourse for a defined set of pre-existing/retained liabilities precisely where the exposure is concentrated, effectively shifting those liabilities onto the client. The aggregate dollar exposure can be material (Schedule 5.2 lists the retained liabilities; the cap reduction compounds the loss).
- Recommended position: REJECT both the cap reduction and the Schedule 5.2 carve-out; restore the base cap and confirm the carve-out is deleted. Concede only the basket mechanics (see Item 5).
- Evidence: Counterparty markup #32; Schedules #84 (Schedule 5.2).

ITEM 2 — Material Adverse Effect Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs (Section 2.1) — RISK: HIGH
- Deviation: The counterparty's markup adds carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action of the exact kind at issue — and Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that fall squarely within those carve-outs.
- Playbook requirement: The playbook requires an unqualified MAE definition (no regulatory-action carve-out) so that adverse regulatory developments attract protection; scheduled exceptions may not re-open the core definition.
- Exposure analysis: Because Schedule 3.7 already documents two pending regulatory inquiries, the newly inserted carve-outs would operate immediately and defeat the MAE protection on the single most live risk that the transaction is meant to address. This is not a theoretical gap — it is a present, quantified regulatory exposure.
- Recommended position: REJECT the regulatory-action carve-outs; restore the base, unqualified MAE definition; confirm Schedule 3.7 does not narrow the definition.
- Evidence: Counterparty markup #32; Schedules #84 (Schedule 3.7).

ITEM 3 — Schedule 5.2 Retained-Liability Shifts (Indemnification/Representation interplay) — RISK: HIGH
- Deviation: The markup's indemnification changes (Item 1) and its treatment of the retained liabilities listed under Schedule 5.2 would silently reallocate those liabilities to the secured party / client.
- Playbook requirement: Retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 must remain with the seller/grantor and must be protected from narrowing by the indemnity provisions.
- Exposure analysis: Without a clean indemnity covering the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, the secured party absorbs those liabilities with no recourse; this is an off-market shift of a defined liability pool.
- Recommended position: REJECT the Schedule 5.2 carve-out; confirm indemnification covers the retained liabilities; retain Schedule 5.2 as a disclosure-only schedule.
- Evidence: Counterparty markup #32; Schedules #84 (Schedule 5.2).

ITEM 4 — Survival / Limitation Period Reduction (Section 8.1) — RISK: HIGH (WALK-AWAY)
- Deviation: The counterparty's markup adds a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations and warranties, contradicting the survival matrix on Exhibit B.
- Playbook requirement: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix; the playbook standard is that the core reps/making survival periods be no shorter than Exhibit B, and any further shortening is unacceptable.
- Exposure analysis: Shortening survival compresses the window within which the secured party may detect and bring claims for breaches of core representations; it directly conflicts with the agreed Exhibit B matrix and the executed credit agreement's indemnity tail.
- Recommended position: REJECT as a walk-away item. Per the controlling partner instruction, any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue — the client will not transact on these terms. Restore Exhibit B survival.
- Evidence: Deal correspondence #110 (controlling instruction); Schedules #84 (Exhibit B); Counterparty markup #32.

ITEM 5 — Basket Conversion (Deductible to Tipping) — RISK: ACCEPT (CONCEDED)
- Deviation: The markup converts the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
- Playbook requirement: The playbook standard is a deductible basket; however, the controlling partner instruction directs the client to concede the conversion.
- Exposure analysis: A tipping basket makes the threshold itself recoverable once breached — marginally adverse to the client but quantifiable and a negotiated concession.
- Recommended position: ACCEPT the tipping-basket conversion per the controlling instruction, but hold firm against all other indemnity/markup items (Items 1, 2, 3, 4).
- Evidence: Deal correspondence #110 (controlling instruction); Counterparty markup #32.

ITEM 6 — Missing Protections / Required Insertions — RISK: MEDIUM
- Missing protections identified against the base materials:
  (a) No representation that the Subject Account is subject to no other/conflicting control agreement (needed for exclusive control under UCC §§ 9-104, 9-314).
  (b) No covenant that the Depository Bank will not terminate the account, change the account number, or transfer the account before notice/control is preserved.
  (c) Control/instruction clause conditional on Grantor/entitlement-holder confirmation in the markup — must be removed so the Bank honors Secured Party instructions without further consent.
  (d) Governing law/jurisdiction tied to the executed credit agreement and the Bank's standard form — not aligned in the markup.
  (e) Account details (Exhibit A) must be guaranteed current and complete.
- Playbook requirement: The depository bank's standard form and the executed credit agreement require all of the above as base protections.
- Recommended position: INSERT all of the above; REJECT the markup's condition on instructions.
- Evidence: Base materials; Depository Bank standard form; executed credit agreement.

================================================================================
II. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
================================================================================

| # | Section | Counterparty Deviation | Playbook/Firm Standard | Risk | Position |
|---|---------|------------------------|------------------------|------|----------|
| 1 | 7.1 (Indemnification) | Reduce indemnification cap; add Schedule 5.2 carve-out | Full base cap; no retained-liability carve-out | HIGH | REJECT |
| 2 | 2.1 (MAE definition) | Add regulatory-action carve-outs (overlap Schedule 3.7) | Unqualified MAE; no regulatory carve-out | HIGH | REJECT |
| 3 | 7.1/5.2 | Silent shift of retained liabilities | Retained liabilities remain with grantor; indemnified | HIGH | REJECT |
| 4 | 8.1 (Survival) | Shorten survival of core reps; contradict Exhibit B | Exhibit B survival matrix | HIGH (walk-away) | REJECT |
| 5 | 7.1 (Basket) | Deductible → tipping basket | Deductible standard | MEDIUM | ACCEPT (per instruction) |
| 6 | 5.1/5.2/6/10 | Missing protections (no conflicting control; no account termination; exclusive instructions; governing law; account details) | Standard form protections | MEDIUM | INSERT / REJECT conflicting terms |

================================================================================
III. CONCLUSION & RECOMMENDATIONS
================================================================================
1. Reject the indemnification cap reduction and the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability carve-out (Items 1 & 3).
2. Reject the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs, which intersect live Schedule 3.7 inquiries (Item 2).
3. Reject the survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue per the controlling instruction (Item 4).
4. Concede the tipping-basket conversion per the controlling instruction (Item 5).
5. Insert the missing control, notice, account-integrity and governing-law protections and restore the exclusive-instruction standard (Item 6).
6. Do not rely on Doc #58 (misfiled unrelated administrative material).

The redlined agreement reflecting these positions is set out in aca-redline.docx.
